extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and enthusiasts of Japanese gardening, floral art, and theatre history/culture
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory guidance and evaluative observations about Japanese floral arrangement, landscape-gardening, garden-party practice, and a brief history/characterization of Japanese theatre (Nō, Kabuki, marionette). Emphasizes aesthetic principles, ritual associations, and social uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of artificiality and pettiness
rubrics_metrics.description: No reasonable amount of feeling can easily prevent an unfavorable judgment on account of the impression of artificiality, pettiness, and excessive devotion to details, without a corresponding largeness of spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs should avoid excessive minutiae that suggest triviality; scale, spirit, and a sense of generosity in composition disarm criticism. Smaller-scale artifices (overly minute replicas, fussy ornament) risk being perceived as petty unless balanced by a larger spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation of quiet, soothing enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Japanese art gives lessons in the quiet, soothing, and refining enjoyment of nature and out-of-door recreations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor modes of pleasure that cultivate gentle appreciation (moon-viewing, cherry-blossom viewing, mushroom-gathering) rather than coarse, exhausting entertainments. The social practices around gardens should encourage contemplation and restrained enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value lies in care of simple natural gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: The secret of Japan’s floral fame and floral enchantment lies rather in the care that her people bestow upon Nature’s simpler gifts than in any transcendent wealth of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize careful cultivation and arrangement of ordinary flora rather than relying on rarity or profusion of wild plants; aesthetic value derives from attentive treatment and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonality and festival-aligned design
rubrics_metrics.description: Flower-viewing excursions and seasonal pastimes form the favourite occupations throughout the year; even snow-viewing is included as one of the flower festivals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange gardens and interior floral displays to reflect the season and calendar of festivals (plum in late winter/early spring, cherry in spring, maples in autumn, etc.). Use seasonal motifs and plan plantings so something is at its height in each season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and prominence of flowerless trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Floral art in Japan makes extensive and effective use of flowerless trees; the most important is the pine, followed by bamboo, willow, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evergreen and structural plants (pines, bamboo, willows) as principal compositional elements; their forms contribute year-round character and are often preferred even in indoor arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive indoor floral arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside-floral arrangements should have regard to the character and uses of the room, to the season, to the nature of the festival or ceremonial occasion, to the other art-objects and furniture, and to the scenery of the garden and remoter landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select materials and style for interior arrangements to harmonize with room function, existing art/furniture, adjoining garden style, and the time of year. Example: contrast with adjoining garden style when desirable; choose moorland-style flowers for certain garden settings and water plants if the garden is waterless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast and harmony using male/female principles
rubrics_metrics.description: It is customary to discriminate between male and female cascades, plants and trees, rocks and stones; distinctions are of forms placed in combination or contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply notions of masculine (bolder, vigorous shapes) and feminine (softer, subsidiary forms) to achieve well-balanced contrasts. Place rocks, falls, and plants in paired or grouped relationships to create gendered contrasts that produce harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and moral associations in plant selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain plants (e.g., lotus) are closely connected with Buddhist religion and associated with spirit-land; this affects their appropriateness for different occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using religiously-associated plants like the lotus for festive decorations; reserve them for obsequies, sacred ceremonies, and contemplative temple settings where symbolic meaning (purity, spiritual growth) is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of miniature representations (bonsai) with fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Single specimens or collections of Bonsai are minute representations of large natural objects and require more tender and intelligent cultural care than most beings receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating bonsai, aim for faithful miniature composition (proportions, trained shapes) that evoke distant scenes; expect long-term, attentive cultivation. Bonsai may be portable and integrated into daily life (e.g., carried by travelers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of gardens into social and daily life
rubrics_metrics.description: In Japan every national festival and almost every social gathering partakes of the character of a garden party; gardens are necessities of living well and happily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design gardens to accommodate social use—verandas, paths, viewing points—and to facilitate customary practices like tea, strolling, and viewing festivals. Public access, temple groves, and common leisure uses should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and plainness in Kobori Enshū school
rubrics_metrics.description: According to their canons everything was to be exceedingly plain and simple; and all the other arts were to be combined in the celebration of the cha-no-yu (tea ceremonies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simplicity in buildings and garden features for tea-ceremony contexts: plain summer-houses, modest pools, rustic bridges, winding paths, and restrained ornament. Combine architectural, horticultural, and decorative arts to serve the tea ritual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rustic features and traditional ornaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Modest pools and artificial streams, plain rustic bridges, winding paths over rude moss-covered stepping-stones, moss-clad hillocks, antique lanterns, and deftly placed islets form characteristic elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate rustic materials and traditional garden ornaments (stone lanterns, stepping-stones, moss) to convey antiquity and naturalness; source antique or regionally-appropriate stones where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planting for continuous seasonal beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Everywhere there are magnificent trees, which were selected so as to have some one species at the height of its beauty at each season of the year (cherry for Spring, maples for Autumn, plum for Winter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose plantings so different species peak in different seasons, ensuring year-round interest and planned succession of spectacles (flowering, foliage color).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and generosity to avoid pettiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The more beautiful modern gardens add something they formerly lacked by allowing a larger freedom from ancient conventions and by introducing foreign elements; large size and generous treatment avoid suggestion of artificiality or pettiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real hills, generous vistas, and varied surfaces when site allows; avoid cramped, overly-miniturized schemes on a scale that reads as artificial unless intentional and masterfully executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic handling of exhibition displays (e.g., chrysanthemums)
rubrics_metrics.description: While individual chrysanthemums can be as fine as elsewhere, the Japanese excel in the culture and development of the whole plant; the artistic character of a show is maintained by elegant and simple arrangement of single flowers as to colour and kindred effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display horticultural specimens with attention to whole-plant form, coordinated color schemes, and simple, elegant staging rather than cluttered, showy presentation. Emphasize development and grouping for visual effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious fusion of native tradition and foreign elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The more beautiful modern gardens retain admirable native features while adding something lacking before, by allowing larger freedom from conventions and introducing foreign elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt and modernize traditional garden vocabulary selectively; introduce foreign design influences to enrich scale, variety, or compositional balance without undermining native aesthetic principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design gardens to offer varied vistas and staged views
rubrics_metrics.description: Paths should lead to high plateaus or vantage points where one can stop at almost every step and admire the change of far-reaching vistas or nearer views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose circuits and paths to reveal changing compositions and framed views; provide sequential experiences so visitors encounter contrasting scenes and focal points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate accompaniment and programing for garden parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Garden parties may include inspection of gardens, exhibitions, music, refreshments, histrionic performances and dances; programmes can be elaborate but should harmonize with garden aesthetics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing events in gardens, balance entertainments and practical accommodations (tents, dry paths, seating, lighting) while preserving visual harmony; avoid overloading the landscape with temporary clutter that competes with the garden's art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nō theatre: prescribed, moral, and poetic performance style
rubrics_metrics.description: Nō acting was in every minutest detail adapted to the words and strictly prescribed; the plays are poetic, often chant-like, contain descriptive parts, and are influenced by Buddhism with little to no immoral suggestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performances should preserve the strict, stylized integration of music, chant, and movement; texts are sung, not spoken, and the moral/religious tone and poetic quality should be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yokyoku and classical drama literary qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Yokyoku (written narrative to be chanted or sung) are not long but strong in the poetical element; some parts cannot be too highly praised despite scholastic defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value poetic strength and evocative description in chanted narratives over extended dramatic dialogue; accept formal constraints that favor musical/lyrical qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kabuki and Shibai class-driven composition and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Kabuki and popular theatres descended from lower social origins; texts were often written to suit performers, frequently altered for practical performance needs, and hence lack high literary merit. Marionette (Shibai) theatre often attains high skill and can be the equivalent of European drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that popular theatre emphasizes performative adaptability and actor-centered text modification; marionette and Jōruri traditions prioritize musical narrative and can be literary and technically sophisticated. For producing popular theatre, prioritize stage effect and performer suitability; for marionette drama, emphasize chanting styles and samisen accompaniment.
